status: frozen before any Earth valley-profile result and before any conditioned map is built
owner_requirement: 'Remember that all of our drawn rivers also have to be there in the eroded map' (7 Nov 2026)

finding_that_motivates_it.old_check: rivers_on_channel = share of drawn-river cells within 1 cell of any >= 200 km2 channel: 1.0 (too loose)

strict_check.cause: the final composition (tier ramps + capped erosion detail + hills) is re-routed with a 4 m burn that is then removed, so nothing keeps the drawn rivers as flow paths

finding_that_motivates_it.outlets: 107 drawn-river components on land; 106 touch the sea or a lake, 1 runs off the map's south edge (the map edge is an outlet, as in the erosion grid)

references: breaching rather than filling across obstacles: Lindsay 2016, Hydrological Processes 30, 846-857 (efficient hybrid breaching-filling); Soille 2004 (carving)
stream burning with a buffer (valley) around the vector streams: Hellweger 1997 (AGREE); Saunders 1999; Lindsay 2016, ESPL 41, 658-668 (stream burning revisited)
drainage of flats and pits: Priority-Flood + epsilon, Barnes, Lehman & Mulla 2014, Computers & Geosciences 62, 117-127
steps: 1. order: geodesic distance g along drawn-river cells (8-neighbour) to an outlet (cell touching sea, lake or map edge)
2. bed R1: upstream to downstream, r = min(z - b0, min over upstream river neighbours (r_u - dec)); floor R = max(r, 1 + 2e-4 (g + 1)) m; dec = max(2e-4 m per px, 8 float32 ulps)
3. valley: non-river land within W px of a river is lowered toward the nearest bed, z' = R + (z - R) (d / W)^p where z > R
4. bed R2 with banks: r additionally <= min over adjacent non-river land of z' - b0; same order and floor
5. banks below R2 + b0 (only where the near-sea floor binds) are raised to R2 + b0
6. Priority-Flood + epsilon (epsilon = max(1e-4 m, 4 float32 ulps)) over all land from the sea, lakes and map edge at 1 m, so every land cell drains; river cells must come out unchanged
method.pixel: map 1.84 km, Earth windows 1.85 km (ETOPO 2022 60 arc-second)

earth_fit_of_the_valley_form.windows: plan_B2 development windows D1-D4 for the fit; B1-B4 reported as a check (they were the B2 blind windows; this valley-profile metric was never computed on them, but they are not unseen data, so this is labelled a check, not a blind test)
earth_fit_of_the_valley_form.reconstruction: the map pipeline on each window: sketch (4 quantile tiers + top-drainage rivers at the map's river density) -> erosion detail (plan_B2 C*) + Earth-fitted hills on the tier ramps, as in terrain_erosion.build_v2 -> conditioning
earth_fit_of_the_valley_form.metric: cross-valley profile: for every 'drawn' river cell, the mean elevation of non-river land at distance d px (rings d = 1..8) minus the river cell's elevation; median over river cells per d. Loss per window = mean over d of |ln((D_rec(d) + 2 m) / (D_true(d) + 2 m))|
earth_fit_of_the_valley_form.selection: the grid point with the lowest mean loss over D1-D4; ties within 0.01 go to the smaller W (less change)
earth_fit_of_the_valley_form.side_effects_reported: plan_B2 M1 divides, M2 slope KS by tier, M3 new-river F1 with and without conditioning (D and B windows)

hard_owner_requirement: 100 % of drawn-river land cells: steepest-descent receiver (D8, float32 as stored) is a drawn-river cell, the sea, a lake or off the map edge
100 % of drawn-river land cells: following receivers stays on drawn-river cells until the sea, a lake or the map edge
0 downstream steps along drawn rivers that climb
100 % of drawn-river land cells lie below every adjacent non-river land cell
do_no_harm: tier band share per tier (the B3 check) drops by no more than 0.02 against height map v2
climate-scale mean |lowpass(z) - lowpass(ramps)| rises by no more than 5 m
tier-1 9 km slope median stays within 10 % of Earth lowlands (0.167 deg)
map_gates.reported: carving depth along rivers (p50 / p90 / p99), raised-bank cells, PF-raised cells; climate-grid river recall (score.river_network_check routing on the 14.7 km grid) with the v2 run's runoff

release: if the hard gates pass, height map v2.1 replaces v2 as the Earth-fit terrain_file; the plan_D climate check is re-run (adopt for the climate unless corrected strict zone agreement drops by more than 0.5 points against v2) and the Earth-fit atlas is rebuilt and republished (release drivers of r44)

amendment_1.status: frozen before any result of the amended method

finding.what: the step-2 bed (breach only: r = min(z - b0, upstream - dec)) collapses to the floor: one low cell of the composition next to the drawn line drags every cell downstream of it down, so upland rivers end up in trenches near sea level
finding.map: height map v2.1 (v1 method): bed lowering p90 193 m, p99 631 m; tier-1 9 km slope median 0.138 deg (gate 0.150-0.184) -> lowland_slope gate failed; owner gates passed
finding.gap: the frozen valley-profile metric is relative to the river and cannot see the bed level; the earlier result (W = 11, p = 1, b0 = 1, at the edge of the grid) is superseded

method: bed reference t: either alpha x tier ramp at the river cell (alpha in grid) or the local valley floor of the composition (minimum within 2 px); at least 1 m

two-sided monotone bed (hybrid breach-fill, Lindsay 2016): lower envelope L by breaching t from the sources down, upper envelope U by filling t from the mouth up, R = (L + U) / 2 (strictly falls downstream; floor as before)
valley within W px: cells above the nearest bed lowered as before; cells below it raised to bed + b0 (no parallel trench beside a drawn river)
banks: every non-river land cell adjacent to a river is at least the highest adjacent bed + b0
Priority-Flood + epsilon as before; owner gates unchanged
amendment_1.metric: joint loss = valley-profile loss (as frozen) + bed loss; bed loss = mean over q in (25, 50, 75) of |ln((rec_q + 0.05) / (true_q + 0.05))| of bed / tier ramp for river cells with ramp > 150 m
amendment_1.selection: lowest mean joint loss over D1-D4; ties within 0.01 go to the smaller W; B1-B4 reported as a check
amendment_1.hill_refit: after the form is chosen, the unmarked-hill height (sigma 1.2, cap 500 m) is refitted on the final conditioned map, height_m in (1000, 1300, 1600, 2000, 2500), by KS of tier-1 9 km slopes against the same Earth lowland reference (output/terrain_erosion_20261107/earth_lowland_slopes.npz), because the final surface is what must match Earth

amendment_2.status: frozen before the scan it governs
amendment_2.finding: Earth-best form (ramp 0.6, W 11, p 1, b0 10) with the hill refit (height 1,600 m, tier-1 slope median 0.170 vs Earth 0.167): owner gates pass, but tier bands fail (tier 3 0.495 -> 0.426, tier 4 0.832 -> 0.805) and the climate-scale change is +5.6 m (limit 5): 20 km valley walls cut into the narrow tier-3 uplands
amendment_2.rule: the do-no-harm gates are constraints (owner: faithful to the tiers): forms are taken in order of mean Earth joint loss on D1-D4; each is screened on the map with the hill height of the first refit (1,600 m); the first that passes all map gates is rebuilt with the full hill refit and adopted if it still passes every gate; otherwise the scan continues down the list
amendment_2.reported: the Earth loss given up against the unconstrained best

amendment_3.status: frozen before the scan it governs

finding.scan_amendment_2: 168 Earth-ranked forms screened at hill height 1,600 m: none passes (best tier-3 share 0.486 vs v2 0.495; climate-scale change >= +5.0 m in all)
finding.decomposition: composition alone with 1,600 m hills: tiers 0.746/0.952/0.452/0.807, scale 51.6 m; with 1,000 m hills: 0.789/0.962/0.487/0.829, 42.2 m. Earth-best valleys on 1,000 m hills: tier-1 slope 0.121 (Earth 0.167). So the hills (added on every tier) are what break the narrow tier-3 band once they must grow to restore lowland slopes the valleys flatten.
finding.note: the Earth valley windows are uplands (B2 chose rugged terrain); the lowland constraint is Earth lowland slopes (hill fit)

changes: unmarked hills only in tier 1 (the owner: "there can be hills outside of the marked heightmap tiers, right now it's all flat"): weight w = clip(2 x gaussian(tier == 1, 3 px) - 1, 0, 1), fading to 0 at the tier-1 edge

tier-1 band share reported only (owner allows hills outside the tiers; as plan_B2 map_v2_B3_revision_1); gates on tiers 2-4 bands (drop <= 0.02 vs v2), climate-scale change (<= +5 m vs v2), tier-1 9 km slope median within 10 % of Earth
scan: forms in order of Earth joint loss; for each, hill height refitted in (1000, 1300, 1600, 2000, 2500) by KS against Earth lowlands; the first form whose refitted map passes every gate is adopted

amendment_4.status: implementation of step 6, after the amendment-3 build
amendment_4.finding: 34 % of land (47 % of tier 1) is flat at the source pixel (steepest drop < 1 cm): closed hollows of the hill layer filled to their spill level (height map v2 had them as undrained pits); Priority-Flood + epsilon drained them in parallel straight lines
amendment_4.change: before Priority-Flood + epsilon, every flat gets increments towards its lower edges and away from its higher edges (Barnes, Lehman & Mulla 2014b, Computers & Geosciences 62, 128-135; Garbrecht & Martz 1997), 2e-4 m per increment; river cells untouched; all gates re-checked
amendment_4.also: drainage areas: fastscapelib accumulate() already multiplies by the cell area, so areas passed as accumulate(dx^2) were m^4. Reported areas, the B3 checks, the previews and plan_B2 M3 now use m^2. Inside evolve() the m^4 numerics are kept because every Earth fit (plan_B2 C*, hill fit, plan_R1) was made with them (verified bit-identical); in them the river boost was inactive (about 0.003 km2) and the first-round rescale clipped. Earlier channel-based checks (rivers_on_channel = 1.0, plan_B2 M3 F1 = 1.00) were therefore not informative.

amendment_5.why: owner: "there is a number of cases on the drawn map where a river goes into a lake then goes back to a river - in the erosion map, they always end at the lake and do not re-start to the sea"
amendment_5.diagnosis: outlets() counted every lake as a river end like the sea, so a river leaving a lake for the sea had water at both ends and split halfway: its upper half drained back into the lake (v2.1 fails the lake-aware check: none of the 11 pass-through lakes drains out, 655 climbing steps)
amendment_5.change: lake network (scripts/terrain_rivers.py lake_network): lakes linked to the sea through drawn rivers are pass-through (rivers flow through them; the geodesic runs through the lake on to the sea); a cluster of lakes with no link to the sea drains into its largest lake (terminal); each pass-through lake is flat at the head of its outflow (stored as lake_level; the atlas loader still zeroes water); shores kept at least b0 above the lake; the strict check takes lake levels and also requires every pass-through lake to drain out

result.note: all changes come from the lake handling (same composition conditioned with and without lakes reproduces v2.1 and v2.2 exactly); about half lie along the lake systems and half are low basins whose fill level follows a changed river bed

amendment_5.simulated_rivers: rotclimate/routing.py: lakes with a level are part of the drainage, so outflows carry the inflows (lake 8 outflow 8.7 -> 1,830 m3/s; lake chain 2-3-5-4 outflow 7 -> 1,069)
